name: AI Content Pipeline - LLM Failover Demo

parameters.content:
## AI Content Pipeline: LLM Failover Demo
Import-ready rebuild of the core pattern from a production 9-agent WordPress publisher (856 posts, zero failed publishes). The signature is **provider failover**: a primary model call with an automatic fallback, so a single provider outage never stops publishing.

**Honest framing:** the production system is custom Python. This is the same architecture in n8n, runnable end to end with zero credentials. Add your own Groq / WordPress keys to make it live.

`Schedule -> Keyword Queue -> Groq (primary) -> [fail?] -> Gemini (fallback) -> SEO -> Publish -> Run Log`

### Keyword Queue (SQLite mirror)
Three sample keyword rows with difficulty + KD type stand in for the production SQLite `keyword_queue`. The pick logic mirrors the KD-rotation rule (favor one hard keyword per two easy).

### LLM Failover (the signature pattern)
**Generate Article - Primary (Groq)** calls `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`. It is set to *Continue On Fail*, so a 401/429/5xx never halts the run.

**IF Primary Failed?** inspects the response. If there is no content, it routes to the fallback.

**Fallback (Gemini)** repeats the request against a different provider and quota pool.

Production cascades further: Groq, then four NVIDIA NIM models, then Gemini. Same idea, more rungs.

### Normalize + SEO Package
**Normalize** unwraps whichever provider answered into one contract: title, article, meta. With no API key it emits a clearly labeled sample article so the pipeline still runs.

**SEO Package** builds the slug, trims the meta description to 155 chars, derives the focus keyword, counts words, and attaches Article schema.

### Publish
**Publish to WordPress (mock)** posts to `httpbin.org` so the demo runs with zero setup and you can see the exact payload echoed back.

**Publish to WordPress (real)** is the official n8n WordPress node, disabled. Add your site credential and enable it to publish for real.

### Run Log + Alerts
**Run Log** writes an outcome summary per run (mirrors the production `post_log` + `agent_runs` tables): keyword, title, provider used, word count, publish status.

**Failure Alert** is a disabled email stub. Wire it to any node's error output for notifications.
